candidates.name: Existing Delivery Cadence engine and shared full/mini payload
candidates.fit_for_gap: Preserve current durable events, fingerprints, gates, hooks and distribution while repairing long transaction locks, work-ahead and publication obligations.

maintenance.last_release: Not established; local source baseline only

evidence.claim: Local source at the linked baseline has exclusive run.lock ownership, sequenced events, snapshot writes and explicit interrupted-tail recovery; withLock awaits the entire supplied action.
Assessment source audit locates global publication admission, one active iteration, long checkpoint ownership, and publication attributed to the newest successful iteration.
Assessment source audit identifies ownership-digest checks for shared payload copying; retain this distribution seam.

risks: Removing publicationDue alone does not solve local-build locking or preserve debt attribution.
A fingerprint does not isolate a mutable checkout.
Shortening transactions requires reload/revision checks before reconciliation; never overwrite concurrent state from an old snapshot.
Full, mini and installed copies differ; do not overwrite user changes.
candidates.decision_rationale: Closest fit to the observed problem, no new daemon or runtime dependency. Extend the existing domain contract rather than replace its persistence or lifecycle.

candidates.name: Existing The Boss GitHub Actions release workflow
candidates.fit_for_gap: Reuse existing native platform jobs and per-platform publication machinery as externally reconciled attempts.

maintenance.runtime_status: Source inspected; no workflow dispatched or verified

evidence.claim: Clean local file defines platform matrix build jobs, immutable sidecar-record inputs, installer manifests, repository_dispatch callbacks and serialized metadata/site publication.
Default concurrency retains only one pending run; queue:max increases pending capacity, but wait order is not dispatch order.
Workflow artifacts can be transferred between jobs and version-4 artifacts are immutable; automatic digest mismatch validation produces a warning, not a mandatory failing gate.

risks: Current publication group omits queue:max; do not treat received callbacks as a durable accounting of all platforms.
Publisher checks the current branch application version; protect version-changing promotion while its prior release is owed.
Workflow availability does not prove candidate identity, platform acceptance, website freshness or successful dispatch recovery.
Remote jobs do not satisfy the mandatory actual local Mac package and new-function operation.
candidates.decision_rationale: Wrap execution references and immutable manifest results into Cadence attempts and obligations. Preserve per-platform incremental publication, one full release at a time and existing publisher-branch contract; no workflow replacement.

candidates.name: p-queue
candidates.fit_for_gap: Optional promise concurrency and admission backpressure inside one already-running Node process.

evidence.claim: Repository search identifies a promise-concurrency queue.
Native ESM queue exposes saturation and queue-size backpressure; its documented unit is an in-process promise task.
Registry reports stable 9.3.3, MIT, ESM and Node >=20, compatible with the declared Node 22+ floor.

risks: Does not itself supply durable cross-process attempt ownership or restart reconciliation.
Adding a long-lived queue owner would conflict with the no-new-daemon requirement.
Would not resolve the currently observed transaction/candidate/publication domain coupling.
candidates.decision_rationale: Useful reference for bounded admission; do not install for this repair. Reconsider only if implementation exposes a concrete within-process queue requirement not already served by the existing harness.

candidates.name: proper-lockfile
candidates.fit_for_gap: Filesystem mutual exclusion and stale-lock detection as a primitive, not durable build ownership.

maintenance.node_engine: No engines constraint published in inspected npm metadata

evidence.claim: Tagged documentation describes mkdir locks, mtime renewal, compromised callbacks, and limitations when locks are manually removed or contenders use inconsistent stale/update settings.
Context7 exposes heartbeat implementation and compromised detection, but reported numeric defaults differ between code and README; no timing setting is adopted here.
Latest published version is 4.1.2, MIT, released in January 2021; runtime compatibility with this project's Windows/Node 22+ path remains unexercised.

risks: A stalled coordinator heartbeat does not prove its compiler or publisher child process stopped.
Lock expiry alone cannot fence stale operation results or prevent an external publication side effect.
Old latest release is a maintenance signal, not proof of abandonment or incompatibility.
candidates.decision_rationale: Retain existing lock primitive for the bounded repair unless an observed deficiency requires replacement. Use the documented failure cases to distinguish transaction locks from operation/resource ownership; no new dependency is justified.

candidates.name: BullMQ
candidates.fit_for_gap: Durable external job queue with workers, completion events and retries.

evidence.claim: Current tag documents Redis-backed queue/worker operation and persistence; live repository description also mentions PostgreSQL, which was not evaluated.
Context7 documents Redis connections for queues and workers; this is not evidence of a daemon-free queue.
Registry stable 6.3.10 is MIT and declares Node >=14.17.0; package compatibility does not satisfy the architecture constraint.

risks: Introduces an unapproved external storage service and worker infrastructure.
Generic job retries cannot establish the safety of replaying uncertain publication effects.
Replacing Cadence still leaves candidate evidence, KBD authorization and obligation semantics to implement.
candidates.decision_rationale: Reject on the no-new-daemon/service boundary, independent of maintenance health. Alternative storage backends do not remove that mismatch.

build_required.need: Candidate-bound work-ahead authorization and immutable multi-repository input manifest
build_required.why_no_candidate: Generic queues do not know the approved KBD parent/change, owned files, dependency classification, real start time or complete production boundary.

build_required.need: Short claim/execute/reconcile transactions for local and per-platform operations
build_required.why_no_candidate: Existing storage is reusable, but stable attempt identity, result ownership/revision checks and reconciliation of unknown external outcomes are Cadence-specific. A queue or lock library alone cannot establish that a previous process stopped.

build_required.need: Candidate-specific publication obligations and monotonic per-platform promotion
build_required.why_no_candidate: CI serialization is not business release ordering or debt coverage. Preserve incremental platform publication, reconcile missed callbacks and protect the existing publisher branch until owed work finishes.

Artifact transfer does not prove command, frozen inputs, exit outcome, artifact identity and actual feature operation. Add an import seam satisfying the same candidate gate; retain unknowns and prevent duplicate dispatch.

build_required.need: Combined count-based obligations and scheduled meaningful-release opportunities
build_required.why_no_candidate: The existing every-two-successful-deliveries policy must remain; session/CI evaluation needs explicit cutoff, eligible delta, skip/hold and debt semantics. No new calendar daemon is needed or permitted.

build_required.need: Compatible state migration, full/mini parity and overlap/backlog reporting
build_required.why_no_candidate: Existing distribution and event primitives can be adapted, but library installation cannot preserve this project's historical evidence, installed-copy ownership or explain unaccepted/pending delivery states.
